judgments.concern: select_detection returns one DetectionCandidate by value, nullopt on an empty list, and throws std::invalid_argument for any strategy other than highest_confidence or largest_area. The rankings are lambdas inside that function: score then area_px, or area_px then score. source_index is not a key. std::max_element keeps the first maximum, and extract_detection_candidates appends in Detection2DArray order, so a tie already resolves to the lower source_index. There is no ranked vector and no Stage2Admission type. A new function can split a copy, and a count of one matches today's winner only when it uses that same comparator and the same first-maximum rule. An unstable sort, or the tail of an ascending stable_sort, admits the other tied candidate. on_pair has no count parameter; detection_selection_ is the only selection input, so the node would pass a literal one. The return value is local to that callback. PalletPoseStamped has no admitted or deferred fields, publish_pose never receives the candidate list, and both diagnostic publishers write only the existing keys plus the two stamps. After the callback returns, the deferred vector is gone, and the handling process still sees one pose or one failure diagnostic and no source indices. Detections with no results, and detections whose class does not match, are already absent from the candidate list, so the two vectors are not a partition of the array. source_index is that array slot for this message. The empty-list case is the existing early return that publishes nothing, and an unknown strategy still throws out of on_pair, which only catches depth_image_to_meters. eval_recorder_node.select_best_detection mirrors the single winner and stores one bbox. With count one and the same strategy, that mirror still matches the admitted candidate and still never records the deferred slots.

on_pair already holds the class-matched candidates and already passes the chosen source_index into estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, which stores it as PoseResult.instance_id and FailureResult.instance_id. publish_pose never reads instance_id. PalletPoseStamped carries the pose, yaw, normal, plane stats, chamfer cost, accepted, an unused quality_reasons string array, failure_reason, provenance, and the two input stamps, and it has no sent index and no deferred list. The deferred indices exist only in the local candidates vector; EstimatePoseOutcome does not carry them, so both publishers have to receive the split from the callback. Adding an int32 and an int32[] at the end of PalletPoseStamped.msg is a change in the one message rosidl_generate_interfaces already builds. The geometry_msgs/PoseStamped published on the same path has no custom fields, so /pps/pallet_pose still cannot carry the roster. On failure the only publication is a DiagnosticStatus of string KeyValues. The two lists have to be encoded as strings, and eval_recorder_node skips OK statuses and stores only failure_reason from WARN, so those keys never enter the report. A reader of PalletPoseStamped alone sees no roster when the estimate fails. The two early returns stay silent: an empty candidate list, and depth_image_to_meters throwing after selection has already computed the split. Those captures stay unmarked. Stage 2 still runs once. The indices are the class-matched slots extract_detection_candidates stored; other array slots are in neither list. The recorder's pose dict keeps yaw and position for one input_rgb_stamp and does not copy new fields, so the report row still has no roster after the message gains them.

The node ranks with detection_selection_, default highest_confidence, which is score then area_px. largest_area is area_px then score and still returns one candidate. Neither comparator uses source_index. The top two by area, then higher score, then lower source_index, is a new ranking. Repeating select_detection with largest_area on a vector left in extract order matches the lower-source-index tie only because max_element returns the first maximum; partial_sort does not. Each admitted face is a full estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2: a full-frame sample_face_points scan, then ransac_plane_fit for up to the default 100 iterations, drawing indices from the node member rng_ seeded at 0. The second call continues that same stream, so its plane depends on how many draws the first face consumed, including early stop, and every later pair on this node is shifted. The prototype cache is a function-local static and stays coherent only while those two calls stay sequential. publish_pose emits both PoseStamped and PalletPoseStamped and does not copy instance_id, so neither pose is tied to a source_index. eval_recorder_node stores one pose per input_rgb_stamp and replaces it when a second rich message arrives, and it records one bbox from select_best_detection using detection_selection, which remains highest_confidence in the node, the launch, and the recorder. The row that survives is the last rich message, and its bbox can be a different detection. There is no deferred message. The messages in this package are PalletPoseStamped and the diagnostic array, plus prototype services. A PalletPoseStamped used as a bare index is stored as a pose. A WARN diagnostic is stored as failure_reason and can mark the sample failed or overwrite a real failure; OK diagnostics are ignored. An admitted face whose estimate fails produces no rich pose and is not deferred, so it is absent from both sides. A pair with fewer than two candidates admits all of them and defers none, which for an empty list is the existing silent return, and a depth conversion throw still publishes nothing after the candidates are known. The detection_selection parameter is then unused by the node while the recorder still applies it.
